High-level asks from you so we can tailor the economics:

- Any hard constraints on model quality vs latency (e.g., never degrade quality vs 1.5x faster).
- A sample set of 20 representative prompts we can use for quantization QA (we can handle redaction).

I suggest we review these options in a short call — I can loop in Karthik for the quantization tradeoffs and Connor for the Dedicated sizing implications.

Quick technical note (summary for commercial):

- Baseline: fp16 inference on our standard v100/nv-core instance (no caching, conservative batching).
- KV / prefix caching: for chat-heavy flows where users reuse system prompts & context fragments, we typically see 15–30% token-cost savings because we avoid re-computing prefixes and can short-circuit model work. Savings skew higher when you have repetitive system instructions or templated responses.
- Dynamic batching: setting an adaptive max latency window (e.g., 30–60ms) yields 10–25% additional token-efficiency on high-concurrency windows while preserving p95 if you set per-route SLAs. Important: tuning is workload-specific — we can provide a recommended initial config.
- Int8 quantization (post-training/inference quant): for many LLaMA-derived variants we see 20–40% throughput improvements with a modest 1–3% delta on our eval BLEU/accuracy proxies on average conversational workloads. For FastCart's accuracy constraints, recommend a phased A/B: run quantized model on 10% traffic for 1 week with your prompt set and automated evals; if regressions >1% on critical intents, rollback / try a mixed precision approach (int8 for latsensitive layers only).
- Combined effect: with aggressive caching + batching + int8, realistic net token-cost reductions are in the 35–55% range for chat-heavy apps. Caveat: embeddings and long-context generation benefit less from batching — embeddings are already cheap on a per-call basis.

Included in attachments: quant-benchmarks-2027-06.csv (model-specific throughput/quality tradeoffs from our internal runs).

Happy to join the customer call to walk through the numbers and the A/B plan.

— Karthik
Senior Applied ML, Redwood Inference

Ellis — thanks for the questions and the patience. Below is a concise commercial package and the technical guardrails we recommend for FastCart's profile.

Commercial options (three alternatives):

1) Starter (no commit) — month-to-month usage at list rates. Optional Optimize Toolkit eval for 30 days free. No liability/penalties.

2) Pilot (recommended to validate economics) — 3-month minimum commit of 300k token-equivalent credits / month (applies to generation + embeddings). Structure: 10% list-rate discount + 50k credit buffer per month for burst usage. If FastCart scales down before 3 months, we limit financial recourse to the remaining unused credits up to 50% of the committed value (capped). Credits can carry forward for one billing cycle. Includes one quantization QA run and a 2-hour tuning session with Karthik's team.

3) Scale (annual reserved) — 12-month commit with tiered volume pricing (starting at 22% off list at the 2M monthly band). Reserved capacity option for predictable p95s and a 2-week on-site/remote tuning and rollout support. Early termination penalties are Material; we will provide explicit numbers if you pick this route.

Technical guardrails (what we will enable if you pick Pilot/Scale):
- Enable KV/prefix caching for frequently repeated system prompts and product templates (expected 15–30% savings).
- Apply adaptive batching with a 40ms default window for chat routes; tune per-route for p95 targets.
- Deploy int8 quantized variant behind a traffic split (10% initial) and run automated regressions on your 20-sample prompt set. If acceptable, escalate to 50% and then full traffic.
- We will instrument token-level cost dashboards and a simple rollback policy (toggle quantized model and cache at runtime).

Next steps:
- If Pilot looks good, can you sign the attached PO stub and we will issue a DocuSign for the pilot SOW? (I added links: HubSpot deal + DocuSign placeholder in the attachments.)
- We propose a 45-minute technical deep-dive with Karthik next Tue to finalize the quant QA plan.

I can soften the Pilot liability cap per your procurement guidance, but prefer to keep a small committed anchor to prioritize capacity.

Regards,
Priyom
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
